subtopic: Plasma Membrane, Cell Wall and Transport
stem:
A unicellular protist X, which has a contractile vacuole to remove excess intracellular water, was placed in a salt solution of increasing osmolarity. The given graph shows the rate of contraction of the vacuole to pump out excess water against the osmolarity of the solution. Select the option that gives the correct explanation of the data.

(The figure is a line graph. The vertical axis reads 'Rate of contraction (Contractions per minute)' and the horizontal axis reads 'Osmolarity of solution (mM)'. The line starts high on the left and falls steadily as it moves right — i.e. the rate of contraction decreases as osmolarity increases.)

options.label: A
options.text: The rate of contraction increases as osmolarity decreases because the amount of water entering X by osmosis increases.

options.label: B
options.text: In an isotonic solution there is no diffusion of water in or out of X, so the contraction rate is zero.

options.label: C
options.text: At higher osmolarity, more salt diffuses into X, therefore lower rates of contraction are required.

options.label: D
options.text: The contractile vacuole is less efficient in a solution of high osmolarity because of reduced respiration and less production of ATP.

stem:
Which of the following is correct for the given figure?

(The figure is a cut-away diagram of a chloroplast. Inside the outer envelope are several stacks of disc-shaped thylakoids (grana). Label 'b' points to one such granum (a stack of discs); label 'a' points into the open ground substance/fluid surrounding the stacks (the stroma); label 'c' points to a membrane connecting two grana, i.e. a stroma/intergranal lamella.)

options.label: A
options.text: The parts labelled 'a', 'b' and 'c', all possess photosynthetic pigments such as chlorophyll.

options.label: B
options.text: The part labelled 'a' is the site of dark reaction.

options.label: C
options.text: The part labelled 'c' is called granum.

options.label: D
options.text: The part labelled 'b' is called intergranal thylakoid.

stem:
Refer to the given figure and select the incorrect statement regarding X, Y and Z.

(The figure is a cut-away diagram of a mitochondrion. Label 'X' points to the smooth outer boundary (the outer membrane); label 'Y' points up into the folded inner membrane projections (the cristae); label 'Z' points to the inner membrane/matrix region on the right.)

options.label: A
options.text: Y contains respiratory enzymes, lipids, RNA, etc.

options.label: B
options.text: Z contains respiratory enzymes, lipids, RNA, etc.

options.label: C
options.text: Y is arranged in a characteristic pattern in different cells and bears oxysomes.

options.label: D
options.text: X is freely permeable to small molecules and ions.

stem:
The kitchen of the cell is:

(Each option is a diagram of a cell organelle. Option A is a lobed bean-shaped body; option B is a set of stacked curved flattened sacs with small vesicles budding off (a Golgi apparatus); option C is a round whorled body; option D is an oval body whose interior contains several stacks of disc-shaped thylakoids — a chloroplast.)

options.label: A
options.text: a lobed, bean-shaped organelle

options.label: B
options.text: a stack of curved flattened sacs with budding vesicles (Golgi apparatus)

options.label: C
options.text: a round, whorled organelle

options.label: D
options.text: an oval organelle containing stacks of disc-shaped thylakoids (chloroplast)

stem:
Among the following cell organelles P, Q, R and S, which is the odd one out?

(The figure shows four organelle diagrams in a row. P is a bean-shaped mitochondrion with internal folds; Q is a rounded nucleus with a dense interior; R is an oval chloroplast containing stacks of disc-shaped thylakoids; S is a cupped, curved sac shape (a Golgi apparatus / dictyosome).)

options.label: A
options.text: S, because the others are membrane bound cell organelles.

options.label: B
options.text: R, because the others are involved in protein storage.

options.label: C
options.text: P, because the others are involved in cell secretion.

options.label: D
options.text: Q, because the others are involved in energy production.

subtopic: Plasma Membrane, Cell Wall and Transport
stem:
Study the given figure carefully. In which direction will the net movement of water take place?

(The figure shows a rectangular container divided into two halves by a dashed vertical line marked 'Semipermeable membrane'. The left half is labelled 'Solution 1' and contains mostly open circles (water molecules) with only a few shaded circles. The right half is labelled 'Solution 2' and is crowded with shaded circles (solute molecules) and fewer open circles. Key: open circle = water molecule; shaded circle = solute molecule. So Solution 2 has the higher solute concentration.)

options.label: A
options.text: From solution 1 to solution 2

options.label: B
options.text: Both from solution 1 to solution 2 and from solution 2 to solution 1

options.label: C
options.text: From solution 2 to solution 1

options.label: D
options.text: No movement will take place

stem:
All members of the Gupta family can roll their tongue. Which of the parts labelled in the given figure carries the information regarding this characteristic?

(The figure is a diagram of a nucleus. A dense rounded body inside is the nucleolus; a network of fine threads fills the interior (chromatin/DNA); the boundary is the nuclear envelope, studded with pores and continuous with rough endoplasmic reticulum. Label P points to the upper envelope/nucleolus region, label Q points to the thread network (chromatin), label R points to the membrane projections on the right, and label S points to the nuclear envelope at the bottom.)

options.label: A
options.text: S

options.label: B
options.text: P

options.label: C
options.text: R

options.label: D
options.text: Q
